  2. defLax606786.Cocycles

    Cocycles and their Lyapunov exponents

    A cocycle consists of an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation σ\sigmaσ of a nonatomic standard probability space (Ω,μ)(\Omega, \mu)(Ω,μ), together with a map ω↦Lω\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omegaω↦Lω​ from Ω\OmegaΩ into the bounded operators on a real Banach space XXX which is

    • strongly measurable: ω↦Lωx\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omega xω↦Lω​x is measurable for each x∈Xx \in Xx∈X;
    • forward integrable: log⁡+∥Lω∥∈L1(μ)\log^+ \|\mathcal{L}_\omega\| \in L^1(\mu)log+∥Lω​∥∈L1(μ).

    No invertibility of Lω\mathcal{L}_\omegaLω​ is assumed. Its iterates are Lω(0)=id\mathcal{L}^{(0)}_\omega = \mathrm{id}Lω(0)​=id and Lω(n+1)=Lσnω∘Lω(n)\mathcal{L}^{(n+1)}_\omega = \mathcal{L}_{\sigma^n \omega} \circ \mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omegaLω(n+1)​=Lσnω​∘Lω(n)​.

    All logarithms below take values in [−∞,∞)[-\infty, \infty)[−∞,∞) with log⁡0=−∞\log 0 = -\inftylog0=−∞. Exponents and multiplicities are indexed from 111, as usual; the value at index 000 is not used.

    • The growth rate of a vector is λω(x)=lim sup⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)x∥\lambda_\omega(x) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega x\|λω​(x)=limsupn​n1​log∥Lω(n)​x∥.
    • The kkk-th Lyapunov exponent (k≥1k \ge 1k≥1) is χk(ω)=lim sup⁡n1nlog⁡ρk(Lω(n))\chi_k(\omega) = \limsup_n \frac1n \log \rho_k(\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega)χk​(ω)=limsupn​n1​logρk​(Lω(n)​), with ρk\rho_kρk​ the Bernstein number. The sequence χ1≥χ2≥⋯\chi_1 \ge \chi_2 \ge \cdotsχ1​≥χ2​≥⋯ is non-increasing and χ1=λ1\chi_1 = \lambda_1χ1​=λ1​ is the top exponent.
    • The distinct exponents λ1>λ2>⋯\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdotsλ1​>λ2​>⋯ are the distinct values of χk\chi_kχk​: λ1=χ1\lambda_1 = \chi_1λ1​=χ1​ and λi+1=χt\lambda_{i+1} = \chi_tλi+1​=χt​ for the least ttt with χt<λi\chi_t < \lambda_iχt​<λi​. The multiplicity mim_imi​ of λi\lambda_iλi​ is the number of kkk with χk=λi\chi_k = \lambda_iχk​=λi​. When there is no exponent after λi\lambda_iλi​ the recursion stops: mim_imi​ is recorded as 000, and the later λ\lambdaλ's are −∞-\infty−∞ (the index at which they would start is recorded as 000, and χ0=−∞\chi_0 = -\inftyχ0​=−∞).
    • The Bernstein index is ν(ω)=lim⁡kχk(ω)=inf⁡kχk(ω)\nu(\omega) = \lim_k \chi_k(\omega) = \inf_k \chi_k(\omega)ν(ω)=limk​χk​(ω)=infk​χk​(ω). It stands in for the usual index of compactness, the growth rate of ∥Lω(n)∥c\|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c∥Lω(n)​∥c​; the concept IndexOfCompactnessIndexOfCompactnessIndexOfCompactness shows that the two agree.
    • The cocycle is quasicompact if ν<λ1\nu < \lambda_1ν<λ1​ almost everywhere.
    • A family of operators ω↦Pω\omega \mapsto P_\omegaω↦Pω​ is tempered if ω↦log⁡∥Pω∥\omega \mapsto \log \|P_\omega\|ω↦log∥Pω​∥ is tempered for (σ,μ)(\sigma, \mu)(σ,μ).

    53
    54/-- A strongly measurable, forward-integrable cocycle of bounded operators on `X` over an
    55invertible ergodic transformation of a Lebesgue probability space. -/
    56structure Cocycle (Ω X : Type*) [MeasurableSpace Ω] [StandardBorelSpace Ω]
    57 [NormedAddCommGroup X] [NormedSpace ℝ X] [MeasurableSpace X] where
    58 /-- The base transformation, a measurable bijection with measurable inverse. -/
    59 σ : Ω ≃ᵐ Ω
    60 /-- The invariant measure. -/
    61 μ : Measure Ω
    62 /-- The generator `ω ↦ 𝓛_ω`. -/
    63 L : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
    64 isProbability : IsProbabilityMeasure μ
    65 nullSingleton : NullSingletonClass μ
    66 ergodic : Ergodic σ μ
    67 stronglyMeasurable : ∀ x : X, Measurable (fun ω => L ω x)
    68 forwardIntegrable : Integrable (fun ω => Real.log (max ‖L ω‖ 1)) μ
    69
    70attribute [instance] Cocycle.isProbability Cocycle.nullSingleton
    71
    72namespace Cocycle
    73
    74/-- `𝓛^{(n)}_ω = 𝓛_{σ^{n-1}ω} ∘ ⋯ ∘ 𝓛_ω`. -/
    75noncomputable def iterate (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → X →L[ℝ] X
    76 | 0, _ => ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ X
    77 | n + 1, ω => (R.L (R.σ^[n] ω)).comp (R.iterate n ω)
    78
    79/-- `λ_ω(x) = limsup (1/n) log ‖𝓛^{(n)}_ω x‖`. -/
    80noncomputable def lambdaAt (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) (x : X) : EReal :=
    81 limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal ‖R.iterate n ω x‖ / (n : EReal)) atTop
    82
    83/-- `χ_k(ω) = limsup (1/n) log ρ_k(𝓛^{(n)}_ω)`. Meaningful for `k ≥ 1`; `χ_0 = -∞`. -/
    84noncomputable def chi (R : Cocycle Ω X) (k : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
    85 limsup (fun n : ℕ => logEReal (bernsteinNumber (R.iterate n ω) k) / (n : EReal)) atTop
    86
    87/-- The index `k` at which the distinct exponent `λ_i` first occurs among the `χ_k`: `1` for
    88`i = 1`, then the least `t ≥ 1` with `χ_t` below `λ_{i-1}`, and `0` once there is none. Index `0` is
    89not used. -/
    90noncomputable def lambdaIdx (R : Cocycle Ω X) : ℕ → Ω → ℕ
    91 | 0, _ => 0
    92 | 1, _ => 1
    93 | (i + 2), ω => sInf {t : ℕ | 1 ≤ t ∧ R.chi t ω < R.chi (R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω) ω}
    94
    95/-- The distinct exponent `λ_i` (for `i ≥ 1`). -/
    96noncomputable def lambda (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : EReal :=
    97 R.chi (R.lambdaIdx i ω) ω
    98
    99/-- The multiplicity `m_i` of `λ_i` (for `i ≥ 1`); `0` if there is no exponent `λ_i`. -/
    100noncomputable def mult (R : Cocycle Ω X) (i : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℕ :=
    101 R.lambdaIdx (i + 1) ω - R.lambdaIdx i ω
    102
    103/-- The Bernstein index `ν(ω) = inf_{k ≥ 1} χ_k(ω)`. -/
    104noncomputable def nu (R : Cocycle Ω X) (ω : Ω) : EReal := ⨅ k : ℕ, R.chi (k + 1) ω
    105
    106/-- `ν < λ₁` almost everywhere. -/
    107def IsQuasicompact (R : Cocycle Ω X) : Prop :=
    108 ∀ᵐ ω ∂(R.μ), R.nu ω < R.chi 1 ω
    109
    110/-- `ω ↦ log ‖P_ω‖` is tempered. -/
    111abbrev IsTempered (R : Cocycle Ω X) (P : Ω → X →L[ℝ] X) : Prop :=
    112 Tempered R.σ R.μ (fun ω => Real.log ‖P ω‖)
    113
    114end Cocycle
    115

  3. thm✓Lax606786.OseledetsDecomposition

    The semi-invertible Oseledets decomposition

    Every cocycle L\mathcal{L}L on a separable Banach space XXX, over an invertible ergodic base (Ω,σ,μ)(\Omega, \sigma, \mu)(Ω,σ,μ), has an Oseledets decomposition (L,(λi),(mi),(Ei),(Vl),(Πl))(L, (\lambda_i), (m_i), (E_i), (V_l), (\Pi_l))(L,(λi​),(mi​),(Ei​),(Vl​),(Πl​)).

    That is, the distinct Lyapunov exponents λ1>λ2>⋯\lambda_1 > \lambda_2 > \cdotsλ1​>λ2​>⋯ and their multiplicities mim_imi​ are almost everywhere constant, and there are measurable equivariant fast spaces Ei(ω)E_i(\omega)Ei​(ω) of dimension mim_imi​ (i<Li < Li<L), growing at rate λi\lambda_iλi​ both in norm and in slowest growth, together with strongly measurable tempered projections Πl(ω)\Pi_l(\omega)Πl​(ω) (2≤l≤L2 \le l \le L2≤l≤L) onto invariant slow spaces Vl(ω)V_l(\omega)Vl​(ω), such that almost surely

    X=E1(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1(ω)⊕Vl(ω),Vl(ω)={x∈X:λω(x)≤λl}.X = E_1(\omega) \oplus \cdots \oplus E_{l-1}(\omega) \oplus V_l(\omega), \qquad V_l(\omega) = \{x \in X : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_l\}.X=E1​(ω)⊕⋯⊕El−1​(ω)⊕Vl​(ω),Vl​(ω)={x∈X:λω​(x)≤λl​}.

    The decomposition is nontrivial (L≥2L \ge 2L≥2) exactly when L\mathcal{L}L is quasicompact.

    By the concepts QuasicompactnessCriterionQuasicompactnessCriterionQuasicompactnessCriterion and IndexOfCompactnessIndexOfCompactnessIndexOfCompactness, this happens if and only if the index of compactness κ=lim⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)∥c\kappa = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_cκ=limn​n1​log∥Lω(n)​∥c​, which always exists, is smaller than λ1\lambda_1λ1​.

    This is Theorem 3 of Lee (2024), a form of Oseledets' multiplicative ergodic theorem (Oseledets 1968; see also Raghunathan 1979, and Ruelle 1979 for compact operators on Hilbert space). Earlier Banach-space versions assumed the operators quasicompact (Thieullen 1987) or injective (Lian and Lu 2010). The semi-invertible form, in which the operators need not be invertible, is due to Froyland, Lloyd and Quas (2010) in finite dimensions and (2013) for quasicompact cocycles on Banach spaces, and to González-Tokman and Quas (2014) on separable Banach spaces.

  4. defLax606786.BanachGrassmannian

    The Grassmannians of a Banach space

    Let XXX be a real normed space. The unit sphere of a subspace V≤XV \le XV≤X is SV={x∈V:∥x∥=1}\mathbb{S}_V = \{x \in V : \|x\| = 1\}SV​={x∈V:∥x∥=1}; it spans VVV, so it determines VVV.

    • The Grassmannian GX\mathcal{G} XGX is the set of closed subspaces V≤XV \le XV≤X admitting a bounded projection X→VX \to VX→V. It carries the distanced(V,W)=dH(SV,SW)∈[0,∞],d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W) \in [0, \infty],d(V,W)=dH​(SV​,SW​)∈[0,∞],the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres (infinite exactly when one of V,WV, WV,W is 000 and the other is not).
    • For k≥0k \ge 0k≥0, GkX\mathcal{G}^k XGkX is the set of V∈GXV \in \mathcal{G} XV∈GX of codimension kkk, that is, with dim⁡(X/V)=k\dim(X/V) = kdim(X/V)=k.
    • For k≥0k \ge 0k≥0, GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X is the set of kkk-dimensional subspaces of XXX. For k≥1k \ge 1k≥1 the unit sphere SV\mathbb{S}_VSV​ is a nonempty compact set and GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X carries the metric d(V,W)=dH(SV,SW)d(V, W) = d_H(\mathbb{S}_V, \mathbb{S}_W)d(V,W)=dH​(SV​,SW​).

    Each is equipped with the Borel σ\sigmaσ-algebra of its distance.

    46 · intro x hx
    47 rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    48 · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    49 · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
    50 rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
    51 rw [hxeq]
    52 refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
    53 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    54 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]

    56namespace Grassmannian
    57
    58/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
    59def sphere (V : Grassmannian X) : Set X :=
    60 Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)
    61
    62/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a closed subset of `X`. -/
    63def toCloseds (V : Grassmannian X) : Closeds X :=
    64 ⟨V.sphere, Metric.isClosed_sphere.inter V.2.isClosed⟩
    65
    66/-- A subspace is the span of its unit sphere, so `V ↦ 𝕊_V` is injective. -/
    67theorem toCloseds_injective : Function.Injective (toCloseds (X := X)) := by
    68 intro V W h
    69 apply Subtype.ext
    70 rw [← span_sphere_inter V.1, ← span_sphere_inter W.1]
    71 exact congrArg (fun s : Closeds X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h
    72
    73/-- The distance on `𝒢X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
    74noncomputable instance instEMetricSpace : EMetricSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
    75 EMetricSpace.induced toCloseds toCloseds_injective inferInstance
    76
    77/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that distance. -/
    78noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace : MeasurableSpace (Grassmannian X) :=
    79 borel (Grassmannian X)
    80
    81instance instBorelSpace : BorelSpace (Grassmannian X) := ⟨rfl⟩
    82
    83/-- `𝕊_V` is closed. -/
    84theorem isClosed_sphere (V : Grassmannian X) : IsClosed V.sphere :=
    85 Metric.isClosed_sphere.inter V.2.isClosed
    86
    87end Grassmannian
    88
    89variable (X)
    90
    91/-- `𝒢^k X`: the subspaces in `𝒢X` of codimension `k`. -/
    92def GrassmannianCofin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
    93 {V : Grassmannian X // FiniteDimensional ℝ (X ⧸ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) ∧
    94 Module.finrank ℝ (X ⧸ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) = k}
    95
    96/-- `𝒢_k X`: the `k`-dimensional subspaces of `X`. -/
    97def GrassmannianFin (k : ℕ) : Type _ :=
    98 {V : Submodule ℝ X // FiniteDimensional ℝ V ∧ Module.finrank ℝ V = k}
    99
    100variable {X}
    101
    102namespace GrassmannianFin
    103
    104/-- The unit sphere `𝕊_V = {x ∈ V : ‖x‖ = 1}`. -/
    105def sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Set X :=
    106 Metric.sphere (0 : X) 1 ∩ (V.1 : Set X)
    107
    108/-- `V` is the span of its unit sphere. -/
    109theorem span_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    110 Submodule.span ℝ V.sphere = (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := by
    111 apply le_antisymm
    112 · exact Submodule.span_le.2 Set.inter_subset_right
    113 · intro x hx
    114 rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
    115 · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    116 · have hxeq : x = ‖x‖ • (‖x‖⁻¹ • x) := by
    117 rw [smul_smul, mul_inv_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0), one_smul]
    118 rw [hxeq]
    119 refine Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.subset_span ⟨?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hx⟩)
    120 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    121 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]
    122
    123/-- `𝕊_V` is compact. -/
    124theorem isCompact_sphere {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : IsCompact V.sphere := by
    125 have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
    126 have himg : V.sphere =
    127 (Subtype.val : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) → X) '' Metric.sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1 := by
    128 ext x
    129 simp only [sphere, Set.mem_inter_iff, Set.mem_image]
    130 constructor
    131 · rintro ⟨hx1, hxV⟩
    132 refine ⟨⟨x, hxV⟩, ?_, rfl⟩
    133 rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hx1 ⊢
    134 · rintro ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩
    135 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm] at hv
    136 exact ⟨by rwa [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm], v.2⟩
    137 rw [himg]
    138 exact (_root_.isCompact_sphere (0 : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X)) 1).image continuous_subtype_val
    139
    140/-- `𝕊_V` is nonempty when `k ≠ 0`. -/
    141theorem nonempty_sphere {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : V.sphere.Nonempty := by
    142 have hne : (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) ≠ ⊥ := by
    143 intro h
    144 apply NeZero.ne k
    145 have hfr := V.2.2
    146 rw [h, finrank_bot] at hfr
    147 exact hfr.symm
    148 obtain ⟨x, hxV, hx0⟩ := Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot hne
    149 refine ⟨‖x‖⁻¹ • x, ?_, V.1.smul_mem _ hxV⟩
    150 rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, norm_smul, norm_inv, norm_norm,
    151 inv_mul_cancel₀ (norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hx0)]
    152
    153/-- `V ↦ 𝕊_V`, as a nonempty compact subset of `X`. -/
    154noncomputable def toNonemptyCompacts {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    155 NonemptyCompacts X where
    156 carrier := V.sphere
    157 isCompact' := V.isCompact_sphere
    158 nonempty' := V.nonempty_sphere
    159
    160/-- A subspace is the span of its unit sphere, so `V ↦ 𝕊_V` is injective. -/
    161theorem toNonemptyCompacts_injective (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    162 Function.Injective (toNonemptyCompacts (X := X) (k := k)) := by
    163 intro V W h
    164 apply Subtype.ext
    165 rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere]
    166 exact congrArg (fun s : NonemptyCompacts X => Submodule.span ℝ (s : Set X)) h
    167
    168/-- The metric on `𝒢_k X`: the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. -/
    169noncomputable instance instMetricSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : MetricSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
    170 MetricSpace.induced toNonemptyCompacts (toNonemptyCompacts_injective k) inferInstance
    171
    172/-- The Borel `σ`-algebra of that metric. -/
    173noncomputable instance instMeasurableSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] :
    174 MeasurableSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) :=
    175 borel (GrassmannianFin X k)
    176
    177instance instBorelSpace (k : ℕ) [NeZero k] : BorelSpace (GrassmannianFin X k) := ⟨rfl⟩
    178
    179/-- `V` is recovered from `𝕊_V`. -/
    180theorem sphere_injective (k : ℕ) : Function.Injective (sphere (X := X) (k := k)) := by
    181 intro V W h
    182 apply Subtype.ext
    183 rw [← V.span_sphere, ← W.span_sphere, h]
    184
    185/-- A finite-dimensional subspace admits a bounded projection onto it, so `𝒢_k X` sits inside
    186`𝒢 X`. -/
    187theorem closedComplemented {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) :
    188 (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X).ClosedComplemented := by
    189 have : FiniteDimensional ℝ (V.1 : Submodule ℝ X) := V.2.1
    190 exact Submodule.ClosedComplemented.of_finiteDimensional _
    191
    192/-- The inclusion `𝒢_k X → 𝒢 X`. -/
    193def toGrassmannian {k : ℕ} (V : GrassmannianFin X k) : Grassmannian X :=
    194 ⟨V.1, V.closedComplemented⟩
    195
    196end GrassmannianFin
    197

  5. thm✓Lax606786.GrassmannianPolish

    The Grassmannian of k-dimensional subspaces is Polish

    Let XXX be a real normed space and k≥1k \ge 1k≥1, and give GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X the Hausdorff distance between unit spheres. If XXX is complete then so is GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X, and if XXX is separable then so is GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X. In particular GkX\mathcal{G}_k XGk​X is Polish when XXX is a separable Banach space. Completeness of spaces of closed subspaces under the gap distance is classical (Kato 2013, Chapter IV, §2.1).

  6. thm✓Lax606786.MeasurableOperatorFamilies

    Measurability of Bernstein numbers and of pushforwards

    Let XXX be a separable real normed space with a σ\sigmaσ-algebra containing the open sets, and let ω↦Aω\omega \mapsto A_\omegaω↦Aω​ be a strongly measurable family of bounded operators on XXX (each ω↦Aωx\omega \mapsto A_\omega xω↦Aω​x measurable). Then for k≥1k \ge 1k≥1:

    • ω↦ρk(Aω)\omega \mapsto \rho_k(A_\omega)ω↦ρk​(Aω​) is measurable, and so is ω↦∥Aω∥\omega \mapsto \|A_\omega\|ω↦∥Aω​∥;
    • ω↦Aωv(ω)\omega \mapsto A_\omega v(\omega)ω↦Aω​v(ω) is measurable for every measurable v:Ω→Xv : \Omega \to Xv:Ω→X (if the σ\sigmaσ-algebra of XXX is Borel);
    • ω↦g(Aω,V)\omega \mapsto g(A_\omega, V)ω↦g(Aω​,V) is measurable for every subspace V≠0V \ne 0V=0, and ω↦g(Aω,E(ω))\omega \mapsto g(A_\omega, E(\omega))ω↦g(Aω​,E(ω)) is measurable for every measurable E:Ω→GkXE : \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_k XE:Ω→Gk​X (if the σ\sigmaσ-algebra of XXX is Borel);
    • if moreover XXX is complete and E:Ω→GkXE : \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_k XE:Ω→Gk​X is measurable, then any F:Ω→GkXF : \Omega \to \mathcal{G}_k XF:Ω→Gk​X with F(ω)=AωE(ω)F(\omega) = A_\omega E(\omega)F(ω)=Aω​E(ω) for every ω\omegaω is measurable.

    For the norm topology on the operators, T↦ρk(T)T \mapsto \rho_k(T)T↦ρk​(T) is itself Borel measurable.

  8. thm✓Lax606786.VolumeGrowthComparison

    Volume growth is comparable to products of Bernstein numbers

    Let XXX be a real normed space and k≥0k \ge 0k≥0. There are constants 0<c≤C0 < c \le C0<c≤C, depending only on kkk, such that for every bounded operator TTT on XXX

    c Dk(T)≤ρ1(T)⋯ρk(T)≤C Dk(T).c\, D_k(T) \le \rho_1(T) \cdots \rho_k(T) \le C\, D_k(T).cDk​(T)≤ρ1​(T)⋯ρk​(T)≤CDk​(T).

    Moreover Dk(ST)≤Dk(S) Dk(T)D_k(ST) \le D_k(S)\, D_k(T)Dk​(ST)≤Dk​(S)Dk​(T), and there is K>0K > 0K>0 depending only on kkk with

    ∏i≤kρi(ST)≤K∏i≤kρi(S)∏i≤kρi(T).\prod_{i \le k} \rho_i(ST) \le K \prod_{i \le k} \rho_i(S) \prod_{i \le k} \rho_i(T).i≤k∏​ρi​(ST)≤Ki≤k∏​ρi​(S)i≤k∏​ρi​(T).

    This is Lemma 8 of Lee (2024); the comparison follows the volume-growth arguments of González-Tokman and Quas (2015). Volume growth is also the basis of Blumenthal's (2016) approach to the multiplicative ergodic theorem.

    such that 1nfn(ω)→C\tfrac1n f_n(\omega) \to Cn1​fn​(ω)→C for μ\muμ-a.e. ω\omegaω. Limits are taken in the extended reals. When the fnf_nfn​ are integrable, Lμ(fn/n)=1n∫fn dμL_\mu(f_n/n) = \tfrac1n \int f_n \, d\muLμ​(fn​/n)=n1​∫fn​dμ.

    The theorem is due to Kingman (1968); the proof follows Steele (1989).

    Let σ\sigmaσ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of a nonatomic standard probability space (Ω,μ)(\Omega, \mu)(Ω,μ).     • the windows Ij(ω)(ω)I_{j(\omega)}(\omega)Ij(ω)​(ω), ω∈A\omega \in Aω∈A, are pairwise disjoint;

  17. thm✓Lax606786.BalancedKingman

    Kingman's theorem for balanced intervals

    Gelfand numbers, Bernstein numbers and the compactness seminorm

    Let XXX be a real normed space, TTT a bounded operator on XXX and k≥1k \ge 1k≥1. Then

    ρk(T)≤sk(T)≤4k−1(k−1)! ρk(T)and∥T∥c≤2k sk(T).\rho_k(T) \le s_k(T) \le 4^{k-1}(k-1)!\,\rho_k(T) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \|T\|_c \le 2k\, s_k(T).ρk​(T)≤sk​(T)≤4k−1(k−1)!ρk​(T)and∥T∥c​≤2ksk​(T).

Sharper constants follow from the Kadec–Snobar theorem (Kadec and Snobar 1971; see also Wojtaszczyk 1991, III.B.10) and from Pietsch's theory of sss-numbers (Pietsch 1974); any constant depending on kkk alone suffices for comparing exponential growth rates.

    The Bernstein index is the index of compactness

    Let L\mathcal{L}L be a cocycle on a separable Banach space XXX. The growth rate of the compactness seminorm (the distance to the compact operators) of the iterates exists almost everywhere and equals the Bernstein index ν=lim⁡kχk\nu = \lim_k \chi_kν=limk​χk​:

    lim⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)∥c=νfor a.e. ω.\lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c = \nu \quad \text{for a.e. } \omega.nlim​n1​log∥Lω(n)​∥c​=νfor a.e. ω.

    Since ν\nuν is almost everywhere constant, the index of compactness κ=lim⁡n1nlog⁡∥Lω(n)∥c∈[−∞,∞)\kappa = \lim_n \tfrac1n \log \|\mathcal{L}^{(n)}_\omega\|_c \in [-\infty, \infty)κ=limn​n1​log∥Lω(n)​∥c​∈[−∞,∞) always exists as an almost-everywhere constant, and ν=κ\nu = \kappaν=κ almost everywhere. This is Lemma 34 of Lee (2024), which assumes that the limit exists; here its existence is part of the statement.

  26. thm✓Lax606786.SlowSpaceNonmeasurability

    Slow spaces on a separable Banach space need not be measurable

    Let Ω=R/Z\Omega = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}Ω=R/Z be the circle with Lebesgue measure, rotated by the irrational angle α=2\alpha = \sqrt2α=2​: σ(ω)=ω+α\sigma(\omega) = \omega + \alphaσ(ω)=ω+α. Let X=ℓ1(Z)X = \ell^1(\mathbb{Z})X=ℓ1(Z) with its Borel σ\sigmaσ-algebra, and e0e_0e0​ its 000-th unit vector. For ω∈Ω\omega \in \Omegaω∈Ω and i∈Zi \in \mathbb{Z}i∈Z let si(ω)=1s_i(\omega) = 1si​(ω)=1 if the representative of ω+iα\omega + i\alphaω+iα in [0,1)[0, 1)[0,1) lies in [0,12)[0, \tfrac12)[0,21​), and si(ω)=−1s_i(\omega) = -1si​(ω)=−1 otherwise, and put

    φω(x)=∑i∈Zsi(ω) xi,Lωx=φω(x) e0.\varphi_\omega(x) = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} s_i(\omega)\, x_i, \qquad \mathcal{L}_\omega x = \varphi_\omega(x)\, e_0 .φω​(x)=i∈Z∑​si​(ω)xi​,Lω​x=φω​(x)e0​.

    Then XXX is separable, and L\mathcal{L}L is a quasicompact cocycle over (Ω,σ)(\Omega, \sigma)(Ω,σ) with λ1=0\lambda_1 = 0λ1​=0 and λ2=−∞\lambda_2 = -\inftyλ2​=−∞. For every ω\omegaω its slow space

    {x∈X:λω(x)≤λ2(ω)}=ker⁡φω\{x \in X : \lambda_\omega(x) \le \lambda_2(\omega)\} = \ker \varphi_\omega{x∈X:λω​(x)≤λ2​(ω)}=kerφω​

    belongs to the Grassmannian GX\mathcal{G} XGX, yet there is no measurable map W:Ω→GXW : \Omega \to \mathcal{G} XW:Ω→GX with W(ω)W(\omega)W(ω) equal to this slow space for every ω\omegaω. So separability of XXX alone does not make the slow spaces of the Oseledets decomposition measurable.

    The mechanism is that of Horan (2020, Remark 4.5.7), who observes that for a family of Perron–Frobenius operators on BVBVBV at mutual distance at least 25\tfrac2552​, measurability of ω↦Lω\omega \mapsto \mathcal{L}_\omegaω↦Lω​ would make arbitrary sets of base points measurable. Lee (2024, Example 35) gives a version over a full shift, on ℓ1(N0)\ell^1(\mathbb{N}_0)ℓ1(N0​) with φω\varphi_\omegaφω​ summing from i=1i = 1i=1; that functional vanishes on e0e_0e0​, so here the sum runs over all coordinates.

    46/-- The rotation angle `α = √2 mod 1`. -/
    47noncomputable def angle : AddCircle (1 : ℝ) := ((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))
    48
    49/-- `s_i(ω) = 1` if the representative of `ω + iα` in `[0, 1)` lies in `[0, 1/2)`, else `-1`. -/
    50noncomputable def sign (ω : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) (i : ℤ) : ℝ :=
    51 if ((AddCircle.equivIco 1 0 (ω + i • angle) : ℝ)) < 1 / 2 then 1 else -1

    56every `ω`. -/
